{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Ono / Array Licence, Development and Supply Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer-side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Array agreement — verified findings only  
**Status:** All findings below carry a "pass" verification (one "repaired") and are drawn solely from the reviewed document.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is, on balance, favourable to us: the licence grant, IP ownership, assignment/change-of-control, exclusivity and supply provisions, minimum-commitment position, MFN, non-solicitation, renewal and post-termination transition regime all sit at or above our position, and the only liquidated damages provision runs in our favour. Governing law is New York — our preferred choice — with an arbitration seat mechanic that, in practice, keeps us at home in Osaka whenever Array commences proceedings.

Six items require attention, three of them in walk-away territory:

- **Critical — no IP infringement indemnity.** Array's indemnity (Section 16.2) does not cover third-party IP infringement, Section 15.4 disclaims non-infringement, and Section 11.4(a) leaves each Party to defend Infringement Actions at its own expense. As licensee we bear all IP risk on compounds and patents Array controls.
- **Critical — no liability cap.** Section 16.5 excludes consequential damages but contains no aggregate cap anywhere in the Agreement. This is a symmetrical gap rather than an adverse asymmetry, but it fails our fallback.
- **High — no customer termination for convenience until launch.** Our at-will right under Section 13.2 does not arise until after First Commercial Sale of both Products, locking us in through the entire development phase.
- **High — one-sided post-termination non-compete** of unspecified duration on us in Section 8.2, with no carve-outs.
- **Medium — uncapped facility inspection right** in Section 4.9(a) (distinct from the acceptable royalty audit in Section 7.4).
- **Medium — no performance or conformance warranty** from Array, coupled with a full implied-warranty disclaimer, leaving us taking supplied Materials effectively "as is".
- **Low — insurance clause missing entirely**, notwithstanding Array's clinical, manufacturing and supply activities.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Indemnification; Recalls (16.2; cf. 15.4, 11.4(a)) | Array's indemnity is limited to its own Territory commercialization, its Clinical Studies and Article 15 breaches; no third-party IP infringement indemnity, non-infringement disclaimed, each Party bears own Infringement Action costs. Fails fallback. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | Patent Prosecution and Enforcement (11.1; 2.1–2.2, 2.6, 4.4, 12.2, 12.6) | We own what our personnel create; no assignment of our IP or Data to Array; exclusive licences with sublicensing rights. Joint Invention restrictions are symmetric and disapplied for the licensed Products; territorial/term limits are the deal bargain. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | General Provisions (18.9, 18.10; cf. 4.5(b)) | Symmetric, with consent-free M&A/successor carve-out for us. Affiliate assignment on consent not unreasonably withheld sits at the fallback. No Array right to terminate or re-price on our Change in Control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Art. IX Product Manufacturing and Supply (9.1(a), 9.4(a)–(b); cf. 8.2) | No sole-sourcing obligation: manufacture and Array supply are rights, not commitments. Section 8.2 is a mutual, category-limited competing-product covenant, addressed under NONCOMPETE. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Art. XIV Effect of Termination (14.3; cf. Arts. VI, VII, 14.5) | The only LD provision runs in our favour (relief from diligence and reduced royalty on Array failure/data concealment). No termination fee or penalty payable by us; only customary late-payment interest. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | Art. II Grant of Licence (2.1–2.2, 2.6; cf. Arts. XIII, 18.9) | Exclusive Development/Commercialization licences plus worldwide non-exclusive Manufacturing licence, consent-free Affiliate sublicensing, third-party manufacturing permitted; converts to perpetual, royalty-free on expiry. Consent gates on Third Party sublicensees are sub-preferred only. |
| High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | Indemnification; Recalls (16.5) | Mutual consequential-damages exclusion with indemnity and gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-outs, but **no aggregate monetary cap anywhere** in the Agreement. Fails fallback; symmetrical, so a gap rather than walk-away. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | Art. VIII Certain Covenants (8.2) | In-term limb acceptable (mutual, Territory-limited, Commercialization-only, category-specific, with royalty-period exit). Post-termination limb is one-sided, of redacted duration, with no internal-development or acquisition carve-outs. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | Term and Termination (13.1–13.2; cf. 13.5, 14.2(a)) | Array has no convenience exit (satisfying that prong), but our at-will right does not arise until after First Commercial Sale of both Products, leaving us locked in through development. Walk-away territory. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Art. IV Development and Regulatory Activities (4.9(a); cf. 7.4) | Royalty audit in 7.4 is at or above fallback (annual, independent firm, Array's cost) — not redlined. Section 4.9(a) allows Array itself to inspect our facilities and records with no frequency cap, no fixed notice and no cost allocation. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions (18.3; cf. 17.3, 17.3(g)) | New York law (preferred), CISG excluded. ICC arbitration seated in Osaka when Array commences and New York when we do; no exclusive foreign seat adverse to us. Provisional relief preserved. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | Art. IX Product Manufacturing and Supply (9.2(b); cf. Arts. VI–VIII) | No MFN or best-terms undertaking by us. The only comparable-terms language runs in our favour (Subcontractor terms to us at least as favourable as those to Array). |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | Art. IX Product Manufacturing and Supply (9.4(a)–(b); cf. Art. VI, 5.1(b)(iii), 8.1(a)) | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, binding forecast or shortfall penalty. Payments limited to upfront, milestones and royalties on actual Net Sales; the sole "shortfall" reference is a royalty true-up. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | Art. VIII Certain Covenants (8.1–8.2) | No non-solicit, no-hire or recruitment restriction anywhere. Article VIII contains only diligence, conflict-of-interest and product exclusivity covenants. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | Term and Termination (13.1–13.2; cf. 1.55, 14.4) | No auto-renewal mechanic; term is expiry-based per Product/country to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term. Section 14.4 confirms post-expiry dealings are not a renewal. No notice window or uplift risk. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | Art. XIV Effect of Termination (14.2(a); 14.5) | Mutual cooperation obligation, defined Wind-down Period, orderly transfer of Regulatory Filings/Data with outside dates, and express cost allocation; Article XIV survives. Noted: no express Array return/destruction of our Confidential Information; Article IX not listed in 14.5 survival. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Representations, Warranties and Covenants (Art. 15; 15.4; cf. Art. IX) | Only Effective-Date representations and forward covenants; no ongoing performance warranty, no conformance/GMP warranty for supplied Materials, no repair/replace/refund remedy, and implied warranties disclaimed. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Indemnification; Recalls (Art. XVI) | No insurance provision anywhere, despite Array conducting Clinical Studies, manufacturing and supplying Product and indemnifying us for Products Liability and clinical trial injury. Below fallback. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

The following are identified in the verified findings as walk-away territory (or, for LOL-CAP, as a fallback failure we treat as a must-fix) and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **No third-party IP infringement indemnity (INDEMN — Section 16.2).** Combined with the Section 15.4 non-infringement disclaimer and the Section 11.4(a) own-expense rule, we carry the full IP risk on Array-controlled compounds and patents. Fails even the fallback.
2. **No customer termination for convenience until first commercial sale of both Products (T4C — Section 13.2).** Expressly in walk-away territory: no at-will exit exists during the multi-year development and pre-launch phase, with only the narrow Section 13.5 Safety/Efficacy rights available.
3. **No performance or conformance warranty, against a full implied-warranty disclaimer (WARRANTY — Article 15/15.4).** We take supplied Materials effectively "as is" with no remedy. Expressly walk-away territory.
4. **Uncapped facility inspection right (AUDIT — Section 4.9(a)).** Unlimited audits are walk-away territory under the rule; the fix is minimal and mirrors mechanics already agreed in Section 7.4.
5. **Complete absence of an insurance covenant (INSURANCE — Article XVI).** Noted in the findings as sitting below the fallback and in walk-away territory for a counterparty performing on-site and data-handling activities.
6. **Post-termination non-compete of unspecified duration (NONCOMPETE — Section 8.2, second limb).** Risks walk-away territory if the redacted anniversary exceeds 12 months; must be quantified.
7. **No aggregate liability cap (LOL-CAP — Section 16.5).** Not walk-away, because the exposure is symmetrical, but it fails the fallback on a material term and we should not sign without a mutual cap.

---

## 4. Next Steps

**Redlines to issue (six items, all with drafted proposals):**

1. **Section 16.2 — add IP indemnity.** Insert a new Section 16.2(e) third-party IP infringement indemnity from Array to us, with customary modification and combination carve-outs, expressly overriding the Section 11.4 cost allocation for such claims. Sections 16.3–16.5 procedure, allocation and consequential-damages provisions already work as standard.
2. **Section 16.5 — add a mutual cap.** Insert a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' payments by us and USD 1,000,000, with confidentiality (Article 10), indemnification (Sections 16.1–16.2), gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap, and confirmation that our payment obligations are not "damages".
3. **Section 13.2 — unlock our convenience exit.** Remove the commencement trigger so we may terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' notice (the fallback notice period, proportionate given the Article XIV transition mechanics).
4. **Section 8.2 — cap the tail.** Cap the post-termination Competing Product restriction at twelve (12) months and add carve-outs for internal research/Development and products acquired through M&A. We accept the in-term limb as it stands.
5. **Section 4.9(a) — bound the inspection right.** Add a once-per-twelve-months cap, thirty (30) days' prior written notice and Array's cost, mirroring Section 7.4.
6. **Article 15 — add a warranty.** Insert a performance/conformance warranty with a 90-day notice window and a re-perform, replace or refund remedy (plus no-malicious-code and compliance-with-law elements), and renumber the disclaimer. No carve-out is needed, as Section 15.4 already opens with "Except as otherwise expressly set forth in this Agreement".
7. **Article XVI — insert insurance.** Add a short Section 16.7 at our preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, product and clinical trial liability USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Array handles our data, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), adapted to the pharma context with a self-insurance option. A mutual clause or the fallback limits are acceptable.

**Redacted terms to confirm with the business before signature:**

- Section 8.2 — duration of the in-term restricted period (should end with the term) and the post-termination anniversary.
- Section 13.2 — the notice period (confirm at 30–90 days).
- Section 7.4 — the notice period and the underpayment percentage triggering cost-shifting.
- Section 14.2(a)(ii) — the bracketed Wind-down Period durations.

**Noted, not redlined (raise only if reopening the relevant article):**

- No express obligation on Array to return or destroy our Confidential Information and Data with a deletion certificate (Section 14.2(a)(vi) is one-directional) — better raised under confidentiality.
- Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival provision, so supply continuity during the Wind-down Period is arguably unaddressed.
- Wind-down and transfer costs allocated to us under Section 14.2(a) operate as economic consequences of an at-will exit; review alongside the Section 13.2 redline rather than separately.

**Sequencing:** we suggest presenting items 1, 3 and 6 (IP indemnity, convenience exit, warranty) as linked must-haves, with the cap (item 2) framed as a symmetrical protection for both Parties, and items 4, 5 and 7 as low-friction conforming edits."}
